newsitem.title: USA: Minn gov, lawmakers meet on education funding plan.
newsitem.headline: Minn gov, lawmakers meet on education funding plan.

text.p: Minnesota Gov. Arne Carlson and state lawmakers reached no agreement Wednesday on plans for a special session to resolve an impasse over education funding.

Minnesota legislators approved a $22 billion biennium budget plan earlier in May, but Carlson has announced plans to veto the $6.7 billion elementary and secondary education package, which does not include tuition credits supported by the Republican governor.
Carlson has proposed $150 million of credits that residents could use for tuition to private schools, parochial schools, tutors, computers for school use and other education-related expenses.

The governor and lawmakers set no agenda for a special session and no date to meet again to resolve the dispute, but spokesman Brian Dietz said Carlson was pleased to lay out his proposal for legislative leaders.
"There may not have been any major accomplishments out of today's meeting, but it is still a step forward because the debate has taken a step forward," Dietz said.

Democratic leaders urged Carlson to sign the education package approved during the regular session and told the governor they could either put his plan up for a vote during a special session or send their original plan back to him, spokesman Tom Smalec said.
House Speaker Phil Carruthers, D-Brooklyn Center, and Senate Majority Leader Roger Moe, D-Erskine, believe Carlson should sign the education plan, which passed with bi-partisan support, Smalec said.
